description: Retrieval probes for the consumer-credit fraud desk. Each probe is a question a human agent would actually need answered mid-call. Probes are content, not code: edit this file to change the benchmark, and nothing in backend/ needs to change.
notes: No memory ids appear here. Ids are assigned by the service and change whenever the corpus is re-seeded, so a benchmark keyed on them would measure nothing after the first re-seed. Relevance is established at run time by labelling the whole in-scope corpus -- see backend/memory_eval/labeller.py.

anchor_terms drive the deterministic cross-check labeller. They are entity strings that a genuinely relevant memory would have to mention. They are deliberately a blunt instrument: they will miss paraphrase, and that is the point -- where the model judge and the anchors agree, the label is solid; where they diverge, the report says so rather than picking a winner.

expected_topics names the engine topic whose description covers the question. It is not used to filter retrieval -- the service does not support topic filtering -- it is used to test whether phrasing a query in the vocabulary the memories were filed under improves recall.

probes.question: When did this customer get back from their trip, and where were they?
probes.intent: An agent needs the actual return date, not the declared end date, before assuming the customer is still abroad.

ground_truth_anchor.why: travel_notices.actual_return_date is authoritative. A memory claiming a different return date is a reconciliation failure, not a retrieval failure.

probes.question: Which card is active on this account right now, and what replaced what?
probes.intent: Before discussing a transaction the agent must know which instrument is live.

ground_truth_anchor.why: cards.status and the replacement chain are authoritative for which card is live.

probes.question: How does this customer want to be contacted, and about what?
probes.intent: Standing contact preference governs how the agent follows up.

ground_truth_anchor.why: customers.preferred_channel is the system of record; the memory should not contradict it.

probes.question: What has the bank already promised this customer, and by when?
probes.intent: An agent must not re-promise or contradict a commitment made on a previous contact.

ground_truth_anchor.why: dispute_events records what the bank actually did, against which a promise can be checked.

probes.question: Which devices and wallets can currently spend on this customer's cards?
probes.intent: A revoked token on a stolen phone is the difference between a safe account and an open one.

ground_truth_anchor.why: wallet_tokens.token_status is authoritative for whether a token can still spend.

probes.question: What charges has this customer disputed, and what happened to each?
probes.intent: The core of the call. Needs the merchant, the amount and the current state of each dispute.

ground_truth_anchor.why: disputes.disputed_amount is authoritative for money. Memory is not a second source of truth for an amount.

probes.question: Why was the previous card closed?
probes.intent: Distinguishes a theft-driven closure from an expiry or a fraud-team freeze.

probes.question: Where was the replacement card being sent?
probes.intent: A card posted to a hotel the customer has already left is a live fraud exposure.

ground_truth_anchor.why: dispute_events records the shipment destination actually used.

probes.question: Has provisional credit been issued, and when is it due?
probes.intent: A regulatory deadline question. The answer differs by regulation path.

ground_truth_anchor.why: disputes.provisional_credit_date is authoritative. Reg Z disputes have no provisional credit requirement at all, so an absent date is an answer, not a gap.

probes.question: Did this customer travel to London?
probes.intent: A deliberate trap. One memory in the corpus says London; the travel_notices table says Lisbon. This probe tests whether retrieval surfaces the contradicted memory, and whether the reconciler then catches it. High retrieval recall here is correct behaviour; presenting the memory as fact is not.

ground_truth_anchor.why: There is no London travel notice. Retrieval should find the memory; the desk should not repeat it.

probes.question: What is this customer's credit limit and current statement balance?
probes.intent: A deliberate negative probe. Nothing in the memory corpus answers this, because a credit limit is warehouse data and does not belong in a memory bank. Retrieval will still return k results -- it always does -- so this probe measures how much irrelevant material a fixed top_k forces into the context window.

ground_truth_anchor.why: This lives in BigQuery. A memory bank that answered it would be storing something it has no business storing.

probes.question: Was there an attempted charge that was blocked rather than completed?
probes.intent: Tests recall of a detail buried mid-sentence in a long consolidated memory rather than stated as its own fact.

ground_truth_anchor.why: authorizations.decision distinguishes a blocked attempt from a posted charge.
